body:
Repeated captures had no reusable disk cache, packaged Chromium paths were lost in browser-commander 0.8, and the dependency ranges retained the extract-zip/fxhash findings and outdated shared Rust types. This PR adds the cache in both packages, fixes packaged browser launching, upgrades dependencies, adds regressions and required dependency-health checks, and prepares the next npm/crates.io releases. It documents the remaining upstream dependency-graph constraints below.

## Requirements and research

The [complete requirement inventory, alternatives, selected plans, root causes and primary upstream references](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/blob/issue-158-fa165d4218b7/docs/case-studies/issue-158/README.md) covers every issue and comment. It compares cacache, http-cache, sha2/tempfile, cargo-outdated and npm outdated. [Reusable probes](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/tree/issue-158-fa165d4218b7/experiments/issue-158) retain the investigations. None of the five defects was already resolved or non-reproducible.

## Changes

- **#153:** Upgrade Puppeteer and puppeteer-core to 25.12.0; extract-zip disappears. The complete lockfile audit now reports zero vulnerabilities, down from 75. Require the moderate-level lockfile audit and freshness job before automatic or manual publication. Document external production Playwright packages for bundled consumers.
- **#154:** Pin JS browser-commander 0.10.0, the first packaged-browser-compatible release requested by the issue. Both-engine unit tests execute the real commander launcher and inspect executablePath/channel at the actual engine calls. Both integration tests render JavaScript HTML with a temporary executable path. [Open blocker #160](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/160) preserves the explicit native-dependency packaging constraint under the freshness policy.
- **#155:** Upgrade scraper to 0.27.0; fxhash is absent from Cargo.lock. Keep the minimal search feature and the full runtime working.
- **#156:** Add public CaptureStore/CachedTransport APIs in JS and Rust: exact bytes and receipts, SHA-256 body deduplication, complete request identity, fetch time, configurable 60-day default TTL, online refresh, strict offline misses, stale flags, versioned JSON import/export, listing and pruning. Both implementations read shared binary and Unicode-header replay fixtures and successfully reuse an actual on-disk capture. Header ordering uses UTF-8 bytes in both implementations. Rust's opt-in cache feature selects no parser, HTTP client or browser. See the [API/format guide](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/blob/issue-158-fa165d4218b7/docs/capture-cache.md).
- **#157:** Update every Rust direct/dev dependency and every JS direct/dev dependency except the documented compatible commander pin. The seven Rust versions are async-tungstenite 0.35.0, base64 0.23.1, browser-commander 0.19.0, reqwest 0.13.5, scraper 0.27.0, tower-http 0.7.1 and zip 8.6.0. Fully update Cargo.lock; enforce registry freshness with live open-issue exceptions and no pending compatible lockfile updates. Prepare Rust 0.4.0/changelog and an npm minor changeset.

## Breaking changes and migrations

- Reqwest 0.13: use `rustls` instead of `rustls-tls`, explicitly enable `query`, and retain charset/cookies/gzip/http2 with default TLS disabled. Native TLS remains opt-in. Current Rust commander removes its previous default OpenSSL route; the dependency guard now rejects every such route.
- async-tungstenite: convert text strings to Utf8Bytes with `.into()` and use its inherent send method. Existing scraper, base64, tower-http, zip and browser wrapper API usage remains compatible and is exercised by the full Rust tests.
- Puppeteer 25: ESM import and await executablePath in browser-install CI; use PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD. Bundled consumers must externalize playwright and playwright-core.
- he 2 and Nock 15: migrate ESM imports across all callers; restore Nock interceptors between Jest VM contexts. Jest 30 uses testPathPatterns throughout CI/docs.
- Babel 8, ESLint 10, jscpd 5 and the remaining tooling are current. Remove redundant assignment/preserve caught error cause for the new lint rules. jscpd now scans real language formats and rejects new clones relative to origin/main, reporting existing clones.
- Node minimum is now 22.22.1; CI/Docker use 24. Docker and scripts use the audited npm lockfile. Yarn Classic cannot resolve the converter's unpublished optional musl binaries. npm's corresponding clean-install regression is handled with the documented 11.13.0 lockfile-generation workaround; current npm ci succeeds. A scoped compatible js-yaml override removes the Istanbul loader's advisory, with coverage verified.
- Docker installers now fail after three unsuccessful package-install attempts, backed by a failing-before/passing-after finite mock test. Rust uses a Bookworm runtime after Bullseye package downloads returned 404s. Docker contexts exclude host build/dependency artifacts; the Rust dependency-caching stage includes the new example.
- Clippy 1.99 requires assertions that expose unexpected collection contents. The matching local toolchain reproduced the CI failure; assertions throughout unit, integration, search and cache tests now compare the complete values while retaining their original conditions.

## Reproduction and validation

Before the changes, the dependency probe found extract-zip and fxhash; both launch-option regressions failed against commander 0.8.1; cache imports/tests failed because the APIs did not exist; registry inventories found the old requirements. Self-review regressions reproduced request mutation during fetching, Unicode-header replay rejection in JS despite a successful Rust import, and the Docker retry failure before their fixes.

Local checks passed:

- Complete JS suite: 516 passing tests, 42 opt-in live tests skipped; five additional Docker endpoint tests passed. Both real browser engines, packaged executable tests, Unicode replay and Docker retry regressions ran.
- JS lint, formatting and duplication policy; clean npm ci; complete moderate-level lockfile audit (zero findings); freshness policy and changeset validation. Cache coverage: 89.23% statements, 77.5% branches.
- Rust all-feature tests: 277 passing tests including doctests; minimal search/cache tests; fmt and Clippy 1.99 across all targets/features with warnings denied; search dependency boundary and default OpenSSL guard.
- Both executable cache examples fetched/replayed identical receipts; the JS example read the Rust-created capture. Package listing includes the replay fixture and example. Fresh-consumer metadata unifies all seven direct dependencies. Cargo update dry-run has zero pending compatible package updates.

The optimized Rust Docker build exceeded the local host's 3 GiB memory budget during generated browser-protocol compilation and was stopped. The [Rust build job on a larger runner](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/actions/runs/37619234486/job/112796233471) passed the release build, package listing and production Docker image using Rust 1.96. The local JS image build and all five endpoint tests also passed.

All 17 checks passed on final commit `9106d26`: [JavaScript checks and live/Docker tests](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/actions/runs/37619234495), [Rust checks, three-platform tests, release and Docker builds](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/actions/runs/37619234486), and [JS/Rust parity, including the ready-for-review rerun](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/actions/runs/37625243866). Full final workflow logs were downloaded and reviewed. Publication jobs are correctly skipped on this pull request. The branch contains the latest `main`, and the working tree is clean.

## Upstream limits and publication

The stronger whole-graph single-copy consumer check still finds upstream copies of async-tungstenite 0.32.1 (chromiumoxide), base64 0.22.1 (chromiumoxide/fantoccini/webdriver), and tower-http 0.6.11 (reqwest). These are ranges in the latest published upstream packages; cargo update cannot cross them. The consumer experiment reports their parents and `--strict` reproduces the remaining failure. This PR unifies this crate's seven direct requirements and does not claim a globally duplicate-free graph.

Release triggers are prepared. Actual npm/crates.io publication runs through the existing protected-main workflows after merge; this branch has not published a release. The two optional musl converter binaries also remain unpublished upstream.

Fixes #153
Fixes #154
Fixes #155
Fixes #156
Fixes #157
Fixes #158
